correctness.rationale: The nonsource harmonic equations are contractive for 0<lambda<1. For hub value X the supports of unselected vertices in empty and singly selected pairs are dX and lambda(1+X)/2. These give the stated hub equation, with positive denominator, and the minima over each occupancy type. In the no-empty-pair case, monotonicity from exactly one source per pair gives X>=d, so the hub does not lower the minimum when a singleton pair remains. Multinomial weights count labeled placements. For d<tau<=lambda a feasible set needs to hit each pair, and the hub-free size-m pattern has minimum d, leaving only the two stated size-(m+1) patterns. Above lambda only the full set works. Evaluating the two remaining hub-free patterns gives beta_m and alpha_m; for example alpha_m-d has numerator 2 lambda^2(1-lambda) over the positive common denominator. The triangle and threshold equalities check out.
residual_risks: Finite reproduction is corroboration; the parameter-uniform claim rests on the equilibrium and occupancy proof.

evidence: Windmill Finding: minimum size 1+mr and two complete families of minimizers, weighted by binomial coefficients and split by the exact internal threshold vartheta. At q=2, b_0=d, b_1=lambda; vartheta for r=0 and r=1 gives beta_m and alpha_m, respectively.

evidence: The windmill proof gives y_s(x)=lambda(x+s)/(q-lambda(q-s-1)), block sums F_s(x)=s+(q-s)y_s(x) and F_q=q, the monotone block ordering, and the hub average. For q=2, F_0=2dx, F_1=1+lambda(1+x)/2, F_2=2. Replace the counts of ordinary and exceptional blocks in the hub average by a,b,c; the scalar equation gives precisely X_{a,b,c}. The least support is the minimum of the hub and the listed block values; when a=0 and b>0 comparing to the one-per-pair fixed point d gives y_1(X)<=X.
